findings.summary: In the default core track, every claim citation link goes nowhere, and the page header's promise that claims are listed at the end is false.
findings.evidence:
cites() (site.rs:169) writes `[{id}]` after statements in all the core sections. The targets are `
  • ` inside "Claims and sources" (line 586). This change marks that section expert and hides it with `.expert{display:none}` unless the checkbox is ticked. An anchor whose target is inside a display:none subtree does not navigate, so on the default page every [cN] link is dead. The header (line 267-268) still says "the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end". Glossary is hidden the same way, although core cards use its terms. This breaks a working default to satisfy the track criterion. Simpler fixes: keep Claims and sources (and Glossary) in the core track and mark truly advanced material as expert instead, or reveal a hidden expert section when one of its children is the link target (`.expert:has(:target){display:block}`). Add a test that every href="#..." in a core section points to an element that is not under class="expert".

findings.summary: The learning path lists only sections that open with the exact text `<section><h2>`. Next steps, About this page and the homepage's job-evidence section are left out, but the design doc says it links "each section".
findings.evidence: learning_path searches for the literal "<section><h2>". Sections written as `<section id="next-steps">`, `<section id="about-this-page">` and `<section id="job-evidence">` (lines 551, 637, 871) never match. docs/design/explainer-site.md says "a learning-path ordered list of links to each section". Matching on the markup text rather than building the list from the section builders is fragile: a future section given an id silently drops out.

findings.summary: On the published homepage, the job-evidence section sits between the header and the new reading-options nav, so the learning path and track switch appear after it.
findings.evidence: finish() inserts the nav right after `</header>`. with_evidence() later inserts the evidence section right after `</header>`, ahead of the nav. The existing test at line 1067 confirms `</header><section id="job-evidence">`.

findings.summary: The text says "every page" gets these features, but the decisions page (xtask/src/decisions.rs:419) has its own wrapper with no skip link, track switch or learning path.
findings.evidence: decisions.rs:419 builds `<body><main>{body}</main></body>` with the shared CSS. Only the CSS rules (focus-visible, reduced-motion) reach it.

summary: All six criteria are met, but the verdict is fail because of one major problem. What works: OLY-B-D2-02 now points at finish() in xtask/src/site.rs, with owner Athena and a measure that names the new test and ends `status: not shown`. The study page gets a skip link, a learning-path list, a core/expert switch that uses no script, `:focus-visible` outlines and a reduced-motion rule, and keeps the viewport meta and dark mode. The new test asserts strings the old page lacked, so it fails without the change. My run of `cargo test -p xtask site` passed (37 tests), and Athena's recorded CI run passed fmt, clippy and the full test suite. The CHANGELOG entry is there. The problem: "Claims and sources" is marked expert and hidden by default, yet every statement in the core sections links to a claim in that hidden section. On the default view all those [cN] links go nowhere, and the header's statement that claims are listed at the end is false; Glossary is hidden the same way. That breaks a working default, so I rated it a major soundness finding. Minor findings: the learning path skips sections that have an id (Next steps, About this page, job evidence); on the homepage the reading options appear below the job-evidence section; and the docs say "every page" though the decisions page has none of the new markup.
